s1.syndrome_frame: Acute neurological presentation with headache, emesis, and dizziness, following a recent surgical procedure
salient_findings: Greenish discharge in the right external auditory canal
Ring-enhancing lesion in the right temporal lobe with gas-fluid level and gas bubbles
key_facts: Recent right tympanomastoidectomy for cholesteatoma 2 months prior
Normal strength in all four extremities
Proteus mirabilis and Enterococcus gallinarum cultured
Fungal, Nocardia, and Actinomyces cultures were negative

raw.syndrome_frame: Acute neurological presentation with headache, emesis, and dizziness, following a recent surgical procedure

differentials: Syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone secretion
Brain abscess due to Burkholderia pseudomallei
per_call: Syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone secretion
Brain abscess due to Burkholderia pseudomallei

shortlist.label: Brain abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Ring-enhancing lesion with gas-fluid level and gas bubbles on CT, consistent with abscess formation

shortlist.label: Otogenic brain abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Recent right tympanomastoidectomy for cholesteatoma and presence of greenish discharge in the right external auditory canal

shortlist.label: Post-surgical brain abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Recent surgical procedure and presence of abscess-like symptoms

shortlist.label: Pyogenic brain abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of Proteus mirabilis and Enterococcus gallinarum in cultures, indicating a bacterial infection

shortlist.label: Cholesteatoma-associated brain abscess
shortlist.why_kept: History of cholesteatoma and recent tympanomastoidectomy, increasing the risk of abscess formation

raw.rationale: Recent right tympanomastoidectomy for cholesteatoma and presence of greenish discharge in the right external auditory canal suggest an otogenic origin of the brain abscess

rejected.label: Brain abscess
rejected.why: Too general, as the case provides specific clues pointing to an otogenic origin

rejected.label: Post-surgical brain abscess
rejected.why: While the patient had recent surgery, the otogenic origin is more specific and relevant to the case

rejected.label: Pyogenic brain abscess
rejected.why: Too general, as the case provides specific clues pointing to an otogenic origin and the presence of specific pathogens

rejected.label: Cholesteatoma-associated brain abscess
rejected.why: While cholesteatoma is relevant, 'otogenic brain abscess' is a more specific and direct diagnosis given the patient's recent tympanomastoidectomy and symptoms
